INTRODUCTION 
 
 
 I, the Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Science & Technology, Environment & Forests, having been authorised by the 
Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this Two Hundr ed Seventy-first 
Report on the Action Taken by the Department of Atomic Energy on the 
recommendations contained in Two Hundred Fifty-sixth Report of the Committee on 
Demands for Grants ( 2015-2016) of the Department of Atomic Energy , which was 
presented/lad in the both the Houses of Parliament on 5th May, 2015. 
 
2. There were Thirty one recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Fifty-
sixth Report of the Committee.  Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the 
Committee were received from the Department on 3rd December, 2015. 
   
3. In the meeting held on 15th January, 2016, the Committee considered the draft 
Report and adopted the same. 
 
 
 
 
 
 ASHWANI KUMAR 
New Delhi: Chairman 
January 15, 2016 Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests 
25 Pausha, 1937 Rajya Sabha 
 

REPORT 
   
 The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the 
Department of Atomic Energy on the recommendations contained in the 
Two Hundred and Fifty-sixth Report of the Department -related 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment 
& Forests on the Demands for Grants (201 5-16) of the Department of 
Atomic Energy, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 5th 
May, 201 5. The Committee had in all made thirty one  
recommendations/observations in the report.  Action Taken Note on the 
report was received by the Committee on 3rd December, 201 5.  The 
Department has accepted all the recommendations of the Committee.  The 
Committee, on examination of Action Taken Notes, is satisfied wit h action 
taken by the Department in respect of recommendations/observations . 
However, the Committee would like the Department to take further action in 
respect of two recommendations as indicated in the Report  (Para Nos. 6.5 
and 7.7). 
 The Committee's reco mmendations, action taken thereon and 
comments of the Committee on the Action Taken by the Department of 
Atomic Energy are set out in the subsequent paragraphs:- 
FINANCIAL PROGRESS IN XII FIVE YEAR PLAN  
Recommendation (Para 6.5) 
 The Committee takes serio us view of the fact that in the first three 
years of current Plan nearly 27% of the allocation have been disbursed.  The 
major share i.e. 73% of the allocation has accumulated for the remaining two 
years.  It seems impossible to utilise 73% of the plan all ocation during the 
remaining two years.  The very purpose of long term planning in the form of 
Five Year Plan comes to a naught. While taking serious view of the fact that 
pro-rata allocations are not made annually, the Committee recommends that 
in the rem aining two years of the Plan period, allocations should be made 
and utilised on pro-rata basis to catch up the Plan targets. 
Action Taken by Government 
DAE accepts the recommendation of the Committee. The 
recommendation has been brought to the notice of Mi nistry of Finance. 
Action Plan is put in place for utilisation of the approved allocation. ID Note 
to the PMO seeking special consideration in the matter of re-appropriation of 
funds for Science & Technology Ministries have also been issued for 
consideration so that approved allocation need not be surrendered for want 
of approvals for the re-appropriation of funds among the Projects. 
Comments 
 The Committee takes note of the reply but would like the 
Department to pursue the matter with Ministry of Finance/P MO 
regularly. 

UTILISATION OF THE APPROVED OUTLAY: A TREND 
Recommendation (Para 7.7 & 7.8) 
 The Committee feels that the budgetary restriction imposed by the 
Ministry of Finance, as pointed by the DAE, was not the only reason for 
reduction in allocation at RE stage in 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15, under-
utilisation of outlay by the Department might have also played a role in 
reduction at R.E. level.  
Action Taken by Government 
The Department accepts the observation of the honourable Committee 
that  the allocation has been under -utilised. The reasons for underutilisation 
has been discussed  and the action plan to overcome this has been chalked 
out in   the  review meeting conducted on 18.06.2015, by Secretary, DAE 
with the Heads of  Units/Aided Institutes/PSUs.  Further, it is submitted here 
that Plan review meetings have been conducted  by Secretary/Additional 
Secretary, DAE periodically. The Department could utilise about 58% of the 
budget under Plan head till October, 2015. 
Comments  
 The Committee takes note of the reply but would like the 
Department to constantly monitor the utilization of funds. 
Recommendation (Para 7.8) 
 The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department needs to 
improve its capability to utilise the allocated resources particularly i n the 
Plan Head through strict monitoring at regular intervals of the physical and 
financial performance of the projects and obviate the possibility of any 
reduction at Revised Estimate Stage. It is felt that considering the strategic 
importance of the institutions of the Department of Atomic Energy, financial 
cuts should be minimized and should not be insisted upon if strategic 
programmes were to be delayed as a result thereof.    
Action Taken by Government 
Department accepts the recommendations of the hon ourable 
Committee.  Action taken in this regard is given below : 
Apart  from  monitoring  at  Unit level/Department  level,  monitoring  
of  the  Plan projects  at micro level has been introduced. This has enabled 
29% of utilisation of the  Plan  expenditure  by  June, 2015  end. The  micro 
level monitoring is likely to  increase the capacity of utilisation of the 
allocation.  Further, it is submitted here that the Department has utilised 58% 
of the budget under Plan head till October, 2015. 
Comments 
 The Committee appreciates the monitoring at micro level besides 
at unit/Department level by the Committee and hopes that this will 
result in increased utilization of allocated resources. 
PROJECTED    DEMAND    AND    APPROVED   OUTLAY   FOR   
2015-16  

VIS-A-VIS 2014-15 
Recommendation (Para 9.8) 
 The Committee feels that reduction at B.E. to the tune of Rs. 6,506.00 
Crores against the projected outlay of Rs. 23,457.00 crore s and especially to 
the tune of Rs. 4109.00 crores under Plan Head against projected Plan BE of 
Rs. 10009.00 crore s in Demand no. 4 substantially. It has adversely 
impacted the Plan projects of the Department. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry of Finance should consider the proposal for 
increase in outlay at RE stage.  
Action Taken by Government 
Department accepts the recommendations of the honourable 
Committee and the recommendations  has  been  brought  to the  notice of  
the Ministry of  Finance for providing sufficient funds at RE 2015 -16 stage 
vide this Office DO No.3/2(4)/2014-Budget/6518 dated 26.05.2015. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of 
the progress  made in the matter. 
IMPACT OF CUT ON PROJECTS 
Recommendations (Para 9.15) 
 The Committee takes note of the fact that the Department had earlier 
also brought to the Committee’s notice a similar reduction of Rs. 957.22 
crores in the non-plan allocation under Demand No. 4, during the Demands 
for Grants for the year 2013 -14, and its adverse effect on the operational 
needs of the Heavy Wate r Plants, Nuclear Fuel Complex and BARC.  The 
Committee had accordingly recommended in its 239 th Report 
(recommendation no.11.2) for the enhancement of allocation.  The 
Department in its Action Taken Note had replied that "the recommendation 
of the Committ ee that the Department's Demand for funds should be 
adequately accommodated to obviate adverse effects on the critical or core 
activities due to shortage of funds" will be brought to the notice of the 
Ministry of Finance at Revised Estimate stage.  
Recommendation (Para 9.16) 
 The Committee expresses its serious concern over the matter that the 
issue has not been resolved yet and has come up again. There has been 
reduction of Rs. 2397.00 Crores in the outlay projected by the Department.  
Recommendation (Para 9.17) 
The Committee finds that despite the fact that the Department has 
been vigorously and forcefully taking up the issue of enhancement of 
allocation for the last three years but the Ministry of Finance had not been 
acceding to the request. In the proce ss, the strategic and crucial programmes 
of the Department are suffering. The Committee recommends that in the 
area of critical national importance, the Ministry of Finance should give 

maximum financial support for the programmes of the Department under the 
appropriate financing mechanism.  
Action Taken by Government 
The  Department  accepts the  concern  of  the  Committee  and  has 
taken up with Ministry   of   Finance   vide  this  Office  DO No.3/2(4)/2014-
Budget/6518  dated 26.05.2015. 
Department accep ts the recommendation of the honourable 
Committee and  the recommendation  has been brought to the  notice of  
Ministry of Finance for their kind consideration. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of 
the progress during Demands for Grants-2016-17. 
BHABHA ATOMIC RESEARCH CENTRE 
Recommendation (Para10.5) 
 The Committee takes note of the increased allocation to BARC, a 
prestigious Research & Development institution and hopes that a concrete 
action plan would be prepared to fully u tilise the allocated budgetary 
resources and important projects would be completed on time. 
Action Taken by Government 
Department accepts the observations of the honourable Committee. 
The action taken in this regard is given below : 
All out efforts are bei ng made to utilize the allocated budgetary resources 
and also to complete the important projects on time. Project review meetings 
are being held at micro level. With this, BARC could achieve utilization of 
funds for more than  99% of RE and FG for the years  2013-14 & 2014 -15.  
During the current financial year (2015 -16) also, as against, approved BE  
provision of Rs.1424.40 crore, the expenditure during first two months 
(April & May, 2015) was 26% of BE. The Monthly Expenditure Plan (MEP) 
targets have also be en met. Further, it is submitted here that BARC has 
utilised 50% of the budget till October, 2015. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the fact that BARC had utilised 99% of 
Revised Estimate 2013 -14 and BE 2014 -15 allocation and could utilise 
50% of the budget t ill October 2015 and hopes that the BARC will 
continue utilizing its entire allocated budget. 
Recommendation (Para Nos.10.8 & 10.9) 
 The Committee notes the contribution of BARC in genetic mutation 
of crop plants using ionising radiation aimed at improved yields, resistant to 
diseases which have resulted in increased and improved production of 
several new crop varieties. Farmers have, thus, far benefitted from over 42 
new crop varieties produced by BARC.  
The Committee is however of the view that the Depart ment's research 
in nuclear agriculture has become more relevant than ever before in today’s 

context when agricultural yields are getting influenced and affected by 
climate change. Therefore, in order to meet challenges, the Department 
should intensify its efforts in developing high-yielding disease-resistant crop 
varieties. 
Action Taken by Government 
The Department accepts the view of the honourable Committee and in 
order  to  meet  the  challenges  in  agriculture,  the  Department  has 
undertaken through Bhabha Atomic Research Centre further R&D work for 
high yielding and disease resistant  pulses, oilseeds, wheat,  and  rice with 3 
more  Agricultural Universities (Raichur, Pantnagar, and Jabalpur) 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply.   
Recommendation (Para 10.11) 
 The Committee, while acknowledging the significance of Bhabha 
Atomic Research Centre (BARC) for popularising and marketing its socially 
beneficial technologies, recommends to the Department to chalk out a 
strategy to market its socially benef icial technologies such as Nisargruna 
Biogas Plant for handling biodegradable wastes; Sludge Hygienization 
Research Irradiation (SHRI) for treatment of municipal sewage, etc. 
including its technology on food preservation, nuclear medicine and 
healthcare, t hrough Technology Transfer & Collaboration Division so that 
base line of their users is increased.   
Action Taken by Government 
The recommendation of the Committee has been accepted by the 
Department and following socially beneficial activities are being progressed.   
1.  Nisagruna technology is being transferred to many techno -
entrepreneurs.  Presently, the number of this technology holders 
is more than 125. There are  about 190 Nisargruna plants 
installed at various locations in the country.   Many Municipal 
Corporations are now coming forward to install decentralized  
Nisargruna plants. BARC has signed MOUs with Municipal 
Corporations of  Chandigarh, Mumbai, Chennai, Rajkot and 
Tuticorin during this year to put up  such plants. State 
Governments of Maharashtra , Goa, Karnataka, Tamilnadu,  
Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh through their Urban Department 
or Pollution Control Boards are interacting with BARC to put 
up more plants for decentralized waste management. Ten plants 
were commissioned in the  year 2014-15. Eight plants would be 
commissioned under MOU with BARC  and other parties this 
year. This is also in line with Swatchh Bharat mission of  the 
Prime Minister.  Recently an MOU has been signed between 
BARC and Ahmedabad  Municipal Corporation to implement 
Dry Sludge Hy gienization Research  Irradiation facility for 

treatment of municipal sewage. Talks are on with   Nagpur and 
Bangalore Municipal Corporations, Punjab Pollution Control  
Board and it is proposed to approach other Municipal 
Corporations of India also to implement this technology.   
2.  Food preservation using irradiation is being popularised by 
making this technology easily accessible in various parts of the 
country. Some of these  plants are now working with full 
efficiency and licences are issued for  irradiating cereals, fruits 
and many agricultural products. These steps will  definitely help 
in increasing the number of users of such irradiated preserved  
12 food. Mangoes have been cleared for export and USA 
permitted to import  irradiated mangoes from our country.  In 
last 4 years, BARC have exported  about 1277 MT of irradiated 
mangoes to USA. Twelve irradiation plants have  been installed 
in public domain so far and 3 plants are functioning in 
Government  sector. 
3.  With regard to nuclear medicine and healthcare, a bout 25% of 
the patients  referred for nuclear medicine 
investigations/treatment are from the East and  North-East of 
India. In view of this, a proposal to set up a full -fledged 
Radiation Medicine Centre at the DAE -VECC Campus in 
Rajarhat, Kolkata, to  provide tertiary nuclear medicine support 
to East and North-East States has been initiated. The centre will 
support the Chittaranjan National Cancer  Institute at Rajarhat, 
Kolkata which is close to the proposed RMC -Kolkata.The 
VECC Medical Cyclotron is expected to be producing FDG by 
mid 2016.   A medical cyclotron will be set up in ACTREC 
Campus at Kharghar to augment the availability of low cost [F -
18] FDG for cancer and other (noncancer) patients. 
4.  During 2014-15, fourteen BARC technologies were transferred 
to 34 private  parties. MOU has been signed between 
Technology Transfer and Collaboration Division of BARC and 
CSIR-Tech, a private company, for  marketing BARC 
technologies. As per the MOU, CSIR -Tech shall promote  
BARC technologies amongst various industrie s and suggest 
suitable industries to BARC for possible technology transfer. 
Comments 
 The Committee while takes note of the reply. 
INDIRA GANDHI CENTRE FOR ATOMIC RESEARCH (IGCAR), 
KALPAKKAM 
Recommendation (Para 11.4) 
 The Committee feels that any curtailm ent of funds for  institutes such 
as  Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research  which is involved in the 

high-end and innovative research in the Fast Breeder Reactor programme 
may slow down the pace of efforts towards second stage nuclear programme 
of developing Fast Breeder Reactor. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that the Department should impress upon the Ministry of Finance to increase 
budgetary allocation to the Centre to enable it to maintain its progress in the 
field of nuclear energy.  The Comm ittee, accordingly, recommends liberal 
financial assistance to the Department. 
Action Taken by Government 
Department  accepts  the observations of the Committee to provide 
sufficient funds to Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) for 
activities of   high-end  and  innovative  research  in the   Fast Breeder 
Reactor programme.  Also recommendations of the Committee have been 
brought to the notice of Ministry   of Finance for providing sufficient funds  
for the above activities of  IGCAR.   Projects have been prioritised and 
additional funds have been provided through first  supplementary by re -

INDIAN RARE EARTHS LIMITED 
Recommendation (Para14.6) 
 The Committee understands that India has second largest Rare Earths 
reserves after China and the prices of Rare Earths have increased 
significantly in the recent past. The Committee feels that the Department 
needs to seriously explore the possibilities of increasing the production of 
Rare Earths and if possible by involving pr ivate sector domestic companies 
forming joint ventures with State -run companies for extraction and 
processing of non -radioactive Rare Earth minerals and selling the same in 
international market.  
Action Taken by Government 
Department accepts the recommenda tions of the  honourable 
Committee.   In this regard, the following are further submitted.   As per the 
data available with USGS 2013, the Rare Earth (RE) reserves in  India is 
about 2.8% of the total explored reserves as against China, Russia & USA  
which have about 50%, 17% & 13% of the total reserves respectively.   It is 

important to note that China had dominated the world market in RE since  
mid 1980s by supplying the material at very competitive price. American & 
European processors of RE shifted their pro duction facilities from their 
respective countries to China for securing the supply chain during the 1990s. 
By 2000, China had captured more than 97% of the world RE market. IREL 
stopped its RE production facility at  RED, Aluva in April 2004 due to 
unfavorable market access considering the abundant cheap product available 
in Indian market.   In view of export controls imposed by Chinese 
Government on exports of RE  products, their market availability has 
substantially dried up and this has resulted in  the prices of RE to increase in 
a progressive manner from 2007 onwards. The RE prices peaked around end 
of 2011 and for certain products such as Cerium &  Lanthanum the price 
went as high as over 100 times the prices prevailing in 2005.   Extremely 
high price of th e product coupled with non -availability of the materials  on 
account of Chinese restrictions have triggered the following:  a) Recycle of 
waste RE bearing material and product containing RE after end of its service 
life b) Intense research looking for reduct ion of use of REs in the end 
product and  search for their substitute in various applications such as 
catalysts, magnets,  ceramics, metal alloys, etc.   From 2012, prices of RE 
started declining and presently the prices of Cerium &  Lanthanum have 
come back t o the levels prevailing in the year 2007. However,  prices of 
some products such as Neodymium, Praseodymium continue to be  
comparatively higher than the prices prevailing in 2007.   Monazite is the 
only commercial source of rare earths in India and it is a  prescribed 
substance as per the notification no. SO 61 (E) dated 18.01.2006 issued  
under the Atomic Energy Act 1962. Non radioactive source of RE minerals 
such as Loparite, Bastnaesite are not available in India.  However, RE is not 
prescribed substance and can freely be imported (without  any restriction) 
under the Industrial Policy.

Recommendation (Para Nos. 18.11 & 18.12) 
 The Committee is of the view that the Department need s to accelerate 
the pace of construction of nuclear reactors and reduce the average 
construction time taken from seven -eight years to five years.  Currently, 
India has an installed capacity of 5,780 MWe of nuclear power, including 
the 1,000 MW of electrici ty being generated by recently inducted Unit -I at

mw are under various stages of construction.  In addition , work on 19 new 
reactors, with a cumulative generation capacity of 17,400 MW, is scheduled

mobilise its resources and intensify its efforts to ensure that the proposed 
nuclear project are completed and commissioned within the scheduled

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science &
Technology, Environment & Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on
its behalf, present this Two Hundred Seventy-second Report on the Action Taken by the Department of
Space on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Fifty-fifth Report of the Committee on
Demands for Grants (2015-16) of the Department of Space, which was presented/laid in both the Houses
of Parliament on 5th May, 2015.
2. There were twenty one recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Fifty-fifth Report of the
Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the
Department on 29th September, 2015.
3. In the meeting held on 15th January, 2016, the Committee considered the draft Report and adopted
the same.
N
EW D ELHI; ASHWANI KUMAR
January 15, 2016 Chairman,

(iv)

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Space on the
recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Fifty-fifth Report of the Department-related
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands
for Grants (2015-16) of the Department of Space, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament
on 5th May, 2015. There were twenty one recommendations in the Report of the Committee. Action
Taken Note on the recommendations of the Committee was received from the Ministry on 29th September,
2015. The Ministry has intimated that it has accepted all the recommendations of the Committee.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
action taken by the Department of Space are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:
FINANCIAL ACHIEVEMENTS OF DEPARTMENT:- AN ANALYSIS OF TREND OF UTILISATION
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the fact that despite the Department of Space being capable of
utilizing 100% of its allocated grants, it has had to face cuts in grants at the R.E. stage in the successive
financial years and the Committee feels that this would delay or disrupt some of  its programmes of
strategic importance to the country. The Committee believes that the Departments such as Space and
Atomic Energy cannot be burdened by resource crunch in the implementation of projects of strategic
importance. The Committee recommends accordingly and the priorities determined by the heads of these
Departments should be respected. (Para 4.2)
Action Taken by Government
The recommendations of the Committee are noted. The views of the Committee will be communicated
to Ministry of Finance during Budget discussions.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of further developments in
this regard.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2015-16
Recommendation
The Committee feels that drastic reduction of Plan components of some of the major programmes
of the Department scheduled for 2015-16 ought not to have been made in view of the strategic
importance of these projects. In fact, there is a case for higher outlays for projects of national importance.
The Committee therefore, recommends that the budget allocation of the Department should be suitably
enhanced at the RE stage. (Para 5.1)

2
Action Taken by Government
The views of the Committee are noted. The Department will review its funding requirements at RE
stage and seek appropriate budget allocations at RE stage depending on programmatic requirements.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that adequate funds are made available to the
Department according to its requirements.
PHYSICAL ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE DEPARTMENT IN 2014-15
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the achievements of the Department in 2014-15. The Department had
successfully placed the spacecraft into the Martian orbit making India the first nation to do so in the
first attempt. The launch of GSLV Mk III experimental flight has demonstrated India's capability of
launching satellites of more than 2 ton capacity. The launch of GSLV D5 exhibits India's might in
developing indigenous cryogenic engine. The Committee hopes that with the launch of the fourth satellite
IRNSS-1D, an independent regional navigation system will be accomplished very soon. These major
achievements of the Department make India a world leader in space technology. (Para 6.2)
Action Taken by Government
The encouraging views of the Committee are noted. The Department will strive towards achieving
greater heights in Space technology in coming years.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes the Department continues to accomplish
achievements in space technology.
POLAR SATELLITE LAUNCH VEHICLES
Recommendation
The Committee expresses its concern over the trend of reduction of B.E. outlay at R.E. stage for
PSLV Projects. The Committee notes that some important launches of PSLV are scheduled during
2015-16 and hopes that PSLV project would not be allowed to be adversely affected this year due to
budgetary constraints. The Committee recommends that the Department of Space utilize the allocated
amount efficiently and in time to have minimal cuts at the R.E. stage to have smooth continuation of
PSLV launches. (Para 10.6)
Action Taken by Government
The recommendations of the Committee are noted. Allocated amount for PSLV continuation programme
will be optimally utilised to ensure timely completion of PSLV launches planned in 2015-16.

3
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITE LAUNCH VEHICLE (GSLV)
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that upgradation and enhancement of GSLV technology is extremely
important for advancement of launch vehicles. The Committee appreciates the launching of GSLV D5
and successful experimental flight of GSLV MK III which has demonstrated India's capability and
progressiveness in developing indigenous cryogenic engines. The Committee, however, feels that improving
the payload performance and advancement of GSLV is needed and recommends that the Department
should take necessary steps in this regard. The Committee also expects the successful launch of GSLV-
D6 in the third quarter of 2015 and the first and second developmental flights i.e. (GSLV MK III - D1)
and (GSLV MK III - D2) in the scheduled time frame of 2016-17 and 2017-18. (Para 11.6)
Action Taken by Government
GSLV-D6/GSAT-6 mission carrying GSA T-6 communication satellite on-board was successfully
launched on 28th August 2015. With this launch, the payload capability of GSLV launch vehicle with
indigenous cryogenic stage has been improved to 2117Kg from 1982Kg (payload mass in GSLV-D5
flight). This improvement was achieved by optimization of Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS) dry mass,
operating of CUS cryogenic engine at higher mixture ratio, improvement of CUS engine efficiency and
optimization of mission strategies.
Further to the successful launch of GSLV experimental flight of GSLV Mk III during December
2014, two developmental flights viz. GSLV MK III-D1 and GSLV MK III-D2 are targeted during
December 2016 & December 2017 respectively. Towards launching of GSLV MK-III-D1 flight, stage
integration for Liquid (L110) stage has started & propellant casting for solid boosters for Solid (S-200)
stages are in progress. Ground testing of CE20 cryogenic engine has been successfully completed.
Vacuum ignition trials of cryogenic engine and ground testing of cryogenic stage along with engine are
the pending activities to be completed before first developmental flight.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee feels that since GSLV MK II is a very crucial launch vehicle with a capability to
put about 4 ton payload to geo-synchronous Transfer orbit, the Department must make all out efforts
to make it successful expeditiously and make full utilization of budgetary resources made available for
this project. Technical hurdles coming in the way must also be overcome so as to ensure that the project
is completed within the scheduled time frame as we are already way behind USA and China in this regard.
(Para 11.11)

4
Action Taken by Government
The GSLV Mk-III is a three stage vehicle with two solid motor strap-ons (S200), a liquid propellant
core stage (L110) and a cryogenic stage (C25). The solid motors and liquid propellant core stages have
been successfully flight tested in sub-orbital mission of GSLV MK-III (LVM3-X) mission during December
2014. This flight validated the operation of vehicle lower stages in the severe aerodynamic and aero-
thermal environments during atmospheric flight and the stage separation systems. Significant achievements
have been made in the development of CE20 cryogenic engine. Integrated Engine (E1) development tests
at sea level conditions successfully completed which validated the structural integrity of engine systems
and demonstrated the repeatability of engine. So far, two cold flow tests and 11 hot tests have been
carried out, which include flight duration hot test for 635Sec, hot test with Mixture Ratio Controller
(MRC) in closed loop and extended duration hot tests with MRC (Mixture Ratio Controller) in closed
loop for 800 Sec.
Development of cryogenic stage (C25) for GSLV MK-III is in advanced stage. Propellant tanks are
realised and engine & stage integration are in progress. The ground testing of C25 cryogenic stage is
expected to be completed during second quarter of 2016. Vacuum ignition trails of cryogenic engine and
ground testing of cryogenic stage along with engine are the pending activities to be completed before
the first developmental flight.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the programme will progress as per its
scheduled time-frame.
TRISONIC WIND TUNNEL PROJECT
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that the Trisonic Wind Tunnel Project is very important to meet the
test requirements for future launch vehicles as it will provide research facility for conducting research tests
for upgrading technology of satellite launch vehicles. However, the Committee as constrained to note that
the inability of the Department to obtain necessary approvals. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the approval of the project should be obtained at the earliest and the Department should ensure that all
necessary efforts are made and adequate funds provided to achieve the desired targets of the project
during 2015-16 and the project is not delayed any further. (Para 12.2)
Action Taken by Government
The project proposal for realisation of Trisonic Wind Tunnel facility has gone through rigorous
internal reviews to firm up the technical specifications of the facility. The project proposal for setting
up the facility is being revised for further processing. During 2015-16, all efforts will be made to obtain
the financial approval for the project.

5
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised about the development in the
matter at the time of examination of Demands for Grants (2016-17) of the Department.
MANNED MISSION/HUMAN SPACE FLIGHT PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee notes that most of the pre-project activities for development of critical technologies
had made significant progress in this critically important mission. However, some of the other critical
technologies like Crew Escape System (CES) and Environment Control and Life Support System (ECLSS)
are still being developed. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should develop
other technologies of the project in an expeditious and time bound manner. The Committee hopes that
the Department would make earnest efforts to optimally utilize the allocation made for the project during
2015-16. (Para 13.5)
Action Taken by Government
Developments of critical technologies for future Human Spaceflight programme such as environmental
and life support system, flight suit & crew escape systems are progressing well. Heat exchangers for
the Thermal & Humidity control system module of Environmental Control and Life Support System
(ECLSS) and five development models and two Engineering models of flight suit have been realised.
The simulation & test facilities like Environment Simulation Chamber (ESC) for the testing of
ECLSS modules & Flight suit systems and Human metabolic CO2 simulator have been realised.
Further development tasks such as Static testing of solid motors used in the Crew Escape System
(CES), Fabrication, testing & qualification of the sub systems for the Crew Module & Crew Escape
System, Fabrication of Service Module simulator & launch pedestal interfaces, Assembly & integration
followed by Launch Pad Abort Test to validate the Crew Escape System and realization, testing and
validation of ECLSS subsystems & improved version of Flight Suit are planned to be completed during
2016-17.
Comments
The Committee notes the progress made in development of manned mission/human space
flight programme and hopes that the Department would be able to complete the ongoing task
of testing and validation of ECLSS subsystems and improved version of flight Suit within its pre
determined schedule.
RADAR IMAGING SATELLITE - RISAT-1A
Recommendation
The Committee is aware that the original target for launch of RISAT-1A with indigenous PSLV
rocket was scheduled for 2017-18 which was later revised to 2019. However, the Committee notes with

6
concern that there has hardly been any progress in the development of RISAT-1A and the project report
is yet to be submitted for necessary approval. The Department of Space has stated that subsequent to
the project approval, it would take about 3 1/2 years to realize the spacecraft. As such, it is amply clear
that the project is way behind schedule. Given the fact that RISAT-1A is an important optical satellite,
relying on sunlight to illuminate the ground below, having many benefits in flood mapping, agriculture
and also glacial studies, the Committee recommends that the Department should make all out efforts for
the completion of the programme even before its scheduled target in 2019, if possible. (Para 15.4)
Action Taken by Government
A project proposal for building and launching RISAT-1A satellite, to ensure data continuity of
C-Band Microwave data of RISAT-1 satellite has been reviewed by Standing Project Appraisal Committee
(SPAC). Based on the recommendations of the committee, the project proposal has been revised and
being processed further for obtaining necessary approvals. The spacecraft is targeted to be launched
during 2018. RISAT-1A is an active microwave remote sensing satellite and does not rely on sunlight to
illuminate the ground below.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee also observes that an amount of 
` 2.00 crores has been allocated to the Mission
this year and the Department had stated that the amount shall be suitably augmented at R.E. stage once
the project is approved. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to ensure its early
approval so as to be able to get adequate funds at R.E. stage. (Para 15.5)
Action Taken by Government
The views of the committee are Noted. The amount of ` 2.00 Crores allocated in BE 2015-16 will
be suitably augmented at RE 2015-16 based on the activities planned during the current financial year.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
INDIAN REGIONAL NA VIGATIONAL SATELLITE SYSTEM (IRNSS)
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that the launching of the remaining satellites of IRNSS will be a great
achievement of Indian Space Programme in accomplishing an independent robust navigation system and
the Committee hopes that the Department will successfully launch the satellites in the scheduled time
frame. The Committee, therefore, recommends that construction of Satellite Control Centre at Hassan,
backup IRNSS Navigation Centre at Lucknow and the backup Satellite Control facility at Bhopal should
be completed at the earliest so that their services are available to the nation without delay .
(Para 17.6)

7
Action Taken by Government
The recommendations of the Committee are noted. As on date, Four navigation satellites viz.
IRNSS-1A, IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1C & IRNSS-1D have already been launched and the remaining three
satellite viz. IRNSS-1E, IRNSS-1F and IRNSS-1G are scheduled for launch before the first quarter of
2016 so that the constellation of Seven satellites is completed. All existing IRNSS satellites are controlled
from Hassan and Bhopal. The primary and backup control functions are already catered to. With regard
to establishing total ground system for controlling all seven satellites with backup ground control centers,
the primary control station at MCF and backup control centre at Bhopal, the work is in progress and
will be completed by first quarter of 2016.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of the work completed by the
Department with regard to the ground control centers.
ASTROSAT MISSION
Recommendation
The Committee is constrained to note that ASTROSAT satellite, which was originally scheduled to
be launched in 2009-10, has not been launched so far. Further, the Department has been reiterating
almost the same reasons for the postponement of the project. The Committee recommends that the
Department should ensure that mission is accomplished in the revised time frame set by the Department.
It is unacceptable that such projects are being repeatedly delayed on account of stated challenges and
reasons that can early be addressed. (Para 19.7)
Action Taken by Government
The ASTROSAT Spacecraft has been successfully launched on-board PSLV-C30 on September 28,
2015. The Department thanks the committee for their valued opinion, and will include development times
and challenges into the schedules for future complex satellites.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
INDIAN LUNAR MISSION - CHANDRAYAAN-2
Recommendation
The Committee is concerned about the reduction in the budgetary allocation for the mission at the
R.E. stage in 2014-15 and also the reduction in allocation to the tune of 
` 20.00 crores in B.E. 2015-
16 as compared to B.E. 2014-15. The Committee recommends that shortage of funds may not be allowed
to adversely affect the completion of the project. (Para 20.5)
Action Taken by Government
Chandrayaan-2 is now reconfigured as a fully indigenous mission with an Orbiter, Lander and Rover
modules. The approval for Revised Cost Estimates of Chandrayaan-2 mission has also been obtained.

8
Payloads for Orbiter, Lander and Rover have been selected and are at various stages of development.
The funding requirements for the mission will be reviewed at RE stage and will be suitably augmented
as per programmatic requirements in order to complete the mission on schedule.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department will take all necessary
measures to complete the mission on schedule.
NASA ISRO SYNTHETIC APERTURE RADAR MISSION (NISAR)
Recommendation
The Committee recommends that keeping in view the importance of the NISAR Mission, the possibility
of preponing its launch before its schedule in 2021 should be explored particularly when components of
the hardware satellite building as well as launch vehicle are likely to be ready before 2019. The
Department should also pursue JPL NASA to accordingly get ready before 2019. (Para 22.3)
Action Taken by Government
ISRO has completed the Baseline Design Reviews (BDR) of Spacecraft and S-band SAR payload
(being developed by ISRO) successfully. ISRO is working on its Spacecraft & S-band SAR realization
schedules to match with L-band SAR payload schedule of JPL, while hoping to work for an earlier
launch (than 2021). This point was discussed during the NISAR Joint Steering Group Meeting held on
July 21, 2015 and will be further pursued with NASA/JPL.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be further apprised of the developments
in the matter.
Recommendation
The Committee notes that an amount of 
` 50.00 crores has been allocated for the NISAR Mission
this year and the Department had hopes that the amount shall be suitably augmented at R.E. stage once
the project is approved. The Committee recommends that adequate funds be provided for expeditious
completion of the Mission. (Para 22.5)
Action Taken by Government
The views of the committee are noted. An amount of ` 50.00 crores has been allocated in BE
2015-16 based on the project milestones envisaged during the current financial year. However, the
Department will review the progress and augment the budget provisions at RE Stage, if necessary.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

9
SATELLITE FOR SAARC COUNTRIES
Recommendation
The Committee notes the benefits that the satellite for SAARC countries would bring about in
matters related to education, tele medicine, disaster response, resource management, weather forecasting
and communication sectors. The Committee feels it will also help foster good relations of India with
SAARC countries. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the approval for realization of this project
may be given at the earliest. (Para 23.4)
Action Taken by Government
DOS/ISRO is making all efforts to realize the satellite for SAARC countries on schedule. Towards
building the satellite, in liaison with Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), a meeting of all SAARC member
nations was convened and the details of the satellite were provided to all member countries. Follow-up
activities in securing concurrence from all members for finalizing the orbital slot and frequency bands
are under progress. After obtaining the concurrence, final approval from the government will be obtained.
Comments
The Committee notes the progress made in the matter and recommends that the Department
should make all out efforts to realize the satellite for SAARC countries on schedule and obtain
the necessary approval from the Government at the earliest.
CONTRIBUTION TO THE SOCIETY
Recommendation
The Committee is disappointed to note that a programme like Educational Communication Unit is
facing cuts in the budget which severely hampers the goal of taking education to the people. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that allocations made for societal programmes should not be reduced
so that the society at large is able to benefit by making full use of the applications of space technologies.
The Committee also takes note of the use of the spin off technologies for socially useful purposes by
the Department. However, the Committee feels that much more needs to be done in view of newer
challenges coming up before the society and the people. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department should review their priorities in this sector to come up to the expectations of the people and
provide them with greater facilities and benefits. (Para 25.4)
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Committee are noted. All efforts will be made by DOS/ISRO to improve
the reach of space based solutions to the common man through societal programmes. DOS/ISRO had
actively coordinated with 60 Central Ministries/Departments in order to find suitable space based solutions
to the problems. About 170 projects across various Ministries/Departments have emerged in the areas
of Natural Resources Management, Energy & Infrastructure, Disaster & Early Warning, Communication
& Navigation, e-Governance & Geo-spatial Governance, Societal Services, and Support to Flagship

10
programmes. One day National Meet on promotion of Space Technology was organised on September
07, 2015 at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi to deliberate on the action plans of various Ministries/Departments.
National Meet has received an overwhelming response with participation of more than 1200 delegates
across 60 Central Ministries/Departments, 28 States and 5 Union Territories. DOS/ISRO will further
pursue the outcomes of the meet.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
DISASTER MANAGEMENT SUPPORT
Recommendation
The Committee feels that unseasonal rains and floods pose great danger to the lives of the people
and cause severe loss of property and damages to crops. As such, there is an urgent need to improve our
Flood Early Warning System. The Committee, therefore, recommends that with the improved observation
capability of our satellites, the capability of the Flood Early warning system should also be improved
at the earliest for securing the lives and property of the people from such unseasonal climatic disasters.
(Para 26.4)
Action Taken by Government
Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) / Department of Space (DOS) has developed methodology
for forecasting flood events using aero-space based inputs and conducted pilot projects in Assam and
Andhra Pradesh. The North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC) is carrying out the Flood Early
Warning System (FLEWS) as an R&D project in Assam State in association with Assam State Disaster
Management Authority (ASDMA). The flood forecasting methodology developed for Godavari basin in
Andhra Pradesh by National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) is transferred to Central Water Commission
(CWC), Hyderabad. Models developed under both of these projects are terrain specific and in addition
to satellite based inputs, in-situ data on rainfall and river discharge at critical points is also required. The
FLEWS model developed for Assam uses meteorological parameters from Indian weather monitoring
satellites for rainfall prediction. The Central Water Commission (CWC), Ministry of Water Resources is
mandated for flood forecasts in India and ISRO is closely working with CWC to increase the lead time
of Early Warning and in extending the models to other flood prone river basins.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply
SPACE PROGRAMME AND INDUSTRY PARTICIPATION
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that participation of industry in the Indian Space Programme is of
utmost importance for various reasons, particularly taking note of the fact that the Department till now

11
has not set up the National Committee which will enhance participation of Industry, the Committee
recommends that the proposed National Committee should be set up without further delay.
(Para 27.3)
Action Taken by Government
In order to evolve a comprehensive strategy to step-up production capacity with industry partnership,
the Department has formed two high-power steering Committees in the areas of Launch Vehicle and
Satellite production.
Among other things, the Committees shall (i) consolidate the requirements for on-going and future
missions and also based on emerging opportunities for space markets, (ii) establish the production profile
for Satellites and Launch vehicles, (iii) assess gap areas in meeting production needs and to work out
broad plans to realize their critical inputs, (iv) create a "Strategy Map" for production, with criteria for
selection of Prime contractors, industry linkages, technology sharing methods, IPR issues, joint ventures,
infrastructure build-up, investment plan, quality assurance support, cost effectiveness, risk mitigation and
other related issues, (v) recommend appropriate structural changes, policy guidelines, procedures, skill
set needs, HR plans etc., (vi) identify critical technologies and collaborations towards selective "self-
reliance" and (vii) recommend an "implementation plan" for ensuring the fulfillment of the objectives
defined with effective review mechanism.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the said Committees would effectively work
towards achieving the mandates assigned to them.
Recommendation
It has been reported that China is exploring the potentiality of solar power at the altitude of 36000
kms. The Committee feels that the Department of Space should also look into such path breaking
initiatives to be a world leader in the field of space. (Para 27.4)
Action Taken by Government
Several space faring nations of the world are reported to be exploring the ways of solar power from
space for past many years. While many studies and experiments have been conducted, as on date such
efforts are not finding any viable solutions. ISRO had done preliminarily studies in this area and is
continuously observing the world scenario. Based on the technological advancement in this area in
understanding the feasibility of generating solar power from space for use on earth will further be
explored.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be updated regarding the efforts of the
Department in exploring ways of generating solar power from space and studies being made in
this regard.

12
Recommendation
The Committee was informed that the Department has the manpower capacity of about 18000 and
around 150-200 are retiring every year. It was also informed that during the last 15 years, manpower
has been increased only once. The last was 5 years back. The Committee feels that in view of the big
strides made and also proposed to be made in various sectors in the area of space, the availability of
adequate, well trained and well equipped manpower is vital. The Committee recommends that while the
Department present its requirement for adequate manpower with cogent reasons keeping the needs of its
future programme and projects, Ministry of Finance must consider the same positively considering the
strategic importance of these projects. The Committee feels that the aim of the Department of Space
should be to establish the position of India as a global leader in its area of operations. The approach
of the government should accordingly be to encourage and facilitate in all manner possible the realization
of this aspirational goal in and of national development and security. (Para 27.5)
Action Taken by Government
Department of Space has drawn up challenging programme during the 12th five year plan, wherein
nearly 58 missions will have to be achieved. While finalising the plan profile, the Department had
estimated an augmentation of 1000 scientific and technical manpower and 100 administrative manpower
to support the increased workload. The Department also constituted two high power committees, with
various domain experts as its members, to take up a detailed work study to assess the optimum level
of manpower augmentation required to support the increased workload of 12th five year plan and
beyond. The recommendations of the work study group for assessing the scientific and technical
manpower has been received and the recommendations of the work study group of administrative
manpower are under finalisation. In addition, the Department also proposed a meagre augmentation of
18 administrative posts to support the project specific requirement of Semi-cryogenic Engine Development
project. Following are the actions completed on the subject:
1. The Department has already submitted a proposal for creation of 18 additional posts to support
the Semi-cryogenic Engine Development project to Ministry of Finance. Ministry of Finance
(MoF) has sought some clarifications, which are being addressed in the Department.
2. The Department is in the process of submitting a proposal for creation of 1000 scientific and
technical manpower to MoF, to support the increased workload arising due to enhanced
activities during 12th five year plan and beyond.
3. The recommendations of the Work Study Group for creation of 100 additional administrative
manpower is underway and a proposal for the same will be submitted to MoF shortly.
Comments
The Committee recommends that to encourage and facilitate the aim of the Department of
Space to establish India as a global leader in space programmes and technology, the Ministry of
Finance should positively consider all the genuine demands of Department of Space for augmenting
its scientific, technical and administrative manpower.
