REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science &
Technology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Fifty-eighth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests
on the Demands for Grants (2015-16) of the Department of Science & Technology, presented to both
the Houses of Parliament on 7th May, 2015. There were twenty recommendations in the Two Hundred
and Fifty-eighth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee
were received from the Department on 13th August, 2015. The Department has intimated that it has
taken action in case of all the recommendations of the Committee. The Committee, on examination of
Action Taken Notes, however is not satisfied with action taken by the Department in respect of seven
recommendations (Para Nos. 7.6, 11.9, 14.10, 16.8, 17.9, 18.3, and 20.10) and would like the Department
to take further action in respect of such recommendations as indicated in the Report.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
Action Taken by the Department of Science & Technology are set out in the subsequent paragraphs:-
TREND OF UTILISATION IN THE LAST THREE YEARS
Recommendation
The Committee finds that though utilisation of allocated resources by the Department improved
considerably in the last three years, the allocation to some of the schemes was reduced due to delay in
seeking administrative approval. The Committee is of the view that grounds cited by the Department are
of routine administrative nature which could have been avoided by the Department as delay in completion
of infrastructure projects leads to time and cost overrun and affects research & development work. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the loopholes which led to underutilisation of funds should be
plugged and delay in seeking administrative approval should be avoided, and also responsibility for
delay should be fixed. (Para 7.6)
Action Taken by Government
The Department has noted the observations of the Committee. Department would make every effort
to seek administrative approvals as early as possible for new projects/schemes to ensure maximum
utilization of funds allocated.
Comments
While taking note of the reply the Committee feels that the Department has not provided any detail
of the steps/measures taken on plugging the loopholes to check underutilisation of funds and fixing
responsibility for delay. The Committee therefore as such reiterates its recommendation and would like
the Department to make a critical review of various factors that led to under-utilisation of funds by the
Department and take necessary concrete measures to plug the loopholes.
MECHANISM TO MONITOR AND REVIEW THE ONGOING SCHEMES
Recommendation
The Committee is of the opinion that a robust monitoring mechanism is essential for ensuring timely
completion of various projects to avoid time and cost overrun and to ensure full utilisation of the

2
allocated funds. The Committee notes the performance of the Department of Science & Technology
evaluated by third party under Result Framework Document and finds that there is a considerable scope
for improvement in the performance and the Department needs to further strengthen its monitoring
mechanism to make it more robust for timely completion of projects and optimum utilisation of funds
in the year 2015-16. (Para 8.3)
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the concern of the Committee for a robust monitoring mechanism for
ensuring timely completion of various projects.
The Department has a sound mechanism for monitoring and evaluation of progress of implementation
of programmes/schemes with the help of external experts. As suggested by the Committee, the Department
would further strengthen the same to make it more robust for timely completion of projects and optimum
utilization of funds in the year 2015-16.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2015-16
Recommendation
The Committee takes strong exception to the fact that despite Department's request for allocation
of more funds, the Ministry of Finance has not paid any heed to the matter in the past two years. Such
constraints only circumscribe the functioning of important projects undertaken by the Department. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that in future the Ministry of Finance should give a favourable
response to the request of the Department. (Para 9.6)
Action Taken by Government
Department has noted the concern of the Committee and would convey it to Ministry of Finance
that the Committee has recommended that the Ministry of Finance.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
MEGA FACILITIES FOR BASIC RESEARCH
Recommendation
It is noted that the Department has adopted and implemented the principle of reciprocity and parity
with regard to the use of mega-facilities in the basic research undertaken by our scientists. This much-
appreciated initiative of the Department is likely to work as an enabler in injecting greater confidence
in our scientists and would also lead to the acknowledgement of our scientific expertise at an international
level. The Committee values the partnership between the DST and the Department of Atomic Energy and
feels that such efforts would develop the much-needed capacity building in the university and academic
sector for building mega facilities for basic research. It will enable the Department to explore possibilities

3
of collaboration with other reputed scientific departments such as the Departments of Biotechnology,
Scientific Research, Space and Ministry of Earth Sciences. The Committee feels that such initiatives need
systematic attention and financial nurturing so that the perennial neglect of basic research in the country
is duly addressed and the systemic pitfalls are avoided. (Para 11.9)
Action Taken by Government
All the Mega Science Projects in progress at the present time are being jointly overseen by the
Secretaries of the DST and the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) on regular basis and necessary
resources are being made available. These will enable our scientists to make forays into advanced
scientific instrumentation at the very cutting edge and open up new and hitherto unexplored domains of
scientific studies. The DST-DAE Cooperation Model has inspired the Department to think of other such
inter-ministerial collaborations with MHRD, DBT, etc.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
INDIA-BASED NEUTRINO OBSERV ATORY PROJECT (INO)
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the joint initiative taken by the Departments of Science & Technology
and Atomic Energy in setting up the India-based Neutrino observatory for cutting-edge research in
Neutrino studies. The Committee wishes all the success to "Asia's first state-of-the-art facility" to provide
research facility in particle physics. Furthermore, the Committee recommends that necessary budgetary
provisions should be made available for the observatory.
The Committee hopes that in the years to come, the observatory will transform into an Observatory
Par Excellence setting international standards and provide high quality research facility to science
students across the country, and help them develop sophisticated detectors and electronics using their own
hands and producing new insights in Neutrino studies. (Para Nos. 12.5 & 12.6)
Action Taken by Government
The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
THIRTY METRE TELESCOPE
Recommendation
The Committee believes that the proposed Thirty Metre Telescope has tremendous potential to
unravel the myriad mysteries of the universe. It is likely to become a tool for the Indian astronomy in
keeping up the level of excellence in research in astronomy and astrophysics of the country. The Committee
hopes that the TMT project would help the country to embark on world class, international science
collaborations and also help develop the required human resources in the field. (Para 13.7)

4
Action Taken by Government
The observation of the Committee has been noted.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
NATIONAL SUPERCOMPUTING MISSION
Recommendation
The Committee finds that India was a leader in Supercomputing till 2005 but it has now slipped
down in the global ranking to 14th place. The Committee is of the view that boosting indigenous efforts
in Supercomputing capability is in strategic interests of India, more so when Information Technology
capabilities of the country are recognised worldwide. The Committee hopes that the mission will help
India attain leadership and self-reliance in the field of Supercomputing. The Committee recommends that
considering the significance of Supercomputing, the Department should make every possible effort
including establishment of requisite ecosystem for the success of the Mission to successfully implement
the project in a time-bound manner. The Committee further recommends that the Department must ensure
that the allocated outlays for the scheme are fully utilised. (Para 14.10)
Action Taken by Government
Subsequent to the approval of the National Supercomputing Mission by CCEA on 25.03.2015, the
officials of the two Departments namely DST & DeitY had several meetings along with the implementing
Institutions namely Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) and Indian Institute of
Science, Bengaluru to finalise the action plan.
The recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee of S&T and E&F have been
accepted for further implementation. Both the Departments have coordinated with the implementation
agencies for success of the Mission within the approved time-lines and the following actions has been
taken:-
1. Administrative Approval for execution of the project entitled "National Supercomputing Mission
(NSM): Building Capacity & Capability" to be implemented jointly by Department of Science
& Technology (DST) and Department of Electronics & Information Technology (DeitY) was
issued on 9th April 2015.
2. A preoperative meeting of NSM co-chaired by Secretary, DeitY and Secretary, DST was held
on 6th May 2015 to discuss and finalize the administrative structure for implementation of the
mission. Officials of DeitY , DST and the two implementing agencies namely IISc and C-DAC
also participated in the meeting.
3. Submission of composition of the Governing Body (GB) by Hon'ble Prime Minister along with
inclusion of names of Scientists is under process for approval of respective Hon'ble Ministers
of both DST and DeitY . The constitution of the GB is under process and is likely to complete
by end of July, 2015.

5
4. The National Supercomputing Mission Executive Board (NSM-EB) has been constituted with
Secretary, DST and Secretary, DeitY as Co-Chairs and the OM has been issued on 04.06.2015.
The first NSM-EB meeting is scheduled for 9th July, 2015 in New Delhi.
5. The Department has already initiated the process for release of initial grant to both the
implementing agencies.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the action taken. The National Mission on Nano Science and
Technology
Recommendation
The Committee finds that fund utilisation under the Mission has been satisfactory in the last eight
years. However, the Committee recommends that the Department should inject the qualitative parameters
in terms of utilization of resources of the National Mission on Nano Science & Technology.
(Para 15.3)
Action Taken by Government
The Department humbly accepts the recommendations of the Committee and will work out details
of utilization of funds under the different objectives of Nano Mission.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised of the details of
qualitative parameters in terms of utilization of resources of the National Mission on Nano
Science & Technology during Demand for Grants 2016-17
Recommendation
The Committee notes with satisfaction that India holds the third rank in terms of publications of
papers on Nano science & technology. The Committee also takes cognisance of the performance of the
Department in the first phase of Nano Mission especially in fundamental sciences and human resources.
The Committee believes that the Department would take necessary steps to achieve the technological
aspects within a timeframe of two years in the second phase of the National Mission on Nano Science
& Technology. (Para 15.10)
Action Taken by Government
DST is grateful for the comments made by the PSC. DST is happy to inform the PSC that it has
already taken several steps to ramp up the technological aspects of Nano Mission in order to achieve
progress in this direction in the remaining duration of the second phase of the Nano Mission. These
include constitution of expert committees to look at projects directed at different stages of technology
development, designing of formats and advertisements for such projects, laying down principles of
cooperation between Nano Mission and Technology Development Board for projects involving loan to
industries, etc.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.

6
IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF RESEARCH IN THE UNIVERSITIES
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken by the Department to increase institutional
capacity for Research in FIST, PURSE, CURIE and SAIF Programmes and the support extended to a
number of universities and colleges for carrying out cutting edge research in their respective field which
has resulted in improvement of performance of the universities. It has been observed that Indian
universities in general, and regional centers based in the hinterland in particular, are deprived of
requisite basic infrastructure and necessary wherewithal to undertake quality research. International
collaboration may be encouraged in such cases, both in terms of developing infrastructure and capacity
building of the personnel. (Para 16.7)
Action Taken by Government
The present ongoing initiatives like FIST, PURSE, SAIF and CURIE are mostly University centric
programmes towards strengthening S&T infrastructure capabilities at University Departments and associated
colleges. However programme like CURIE, PURSE are pro-active form of support to enhance the
research capacities at the Universities and exclusive for Universities. These include Universities of all
categories and represents from all parts of country. In fact, in last 2 years or so, a few sophisticated
Analytical Instrument Facilities (SAIF), have been set at 2nd tier Universities like GG Viswavidyalaya,
Bilaspur, Karnataka University, Dharward, Shivaji University Kolhapur, etc., for augmentation of research
facilities for the researchers at remote locations.
Similarly, in FIST Programme, nearly 2150 University Departments and more than 330 PG Colleges
have so far covered for support. However, a step up approach in respect of covering more PG Colleges
and Universities from less endowed places is being taken. In fact, all these initiatives have resulted in
increase in publication Share from University sector as well as positioning of currently more than 3330
(75% of 4500 INSPIRE Fellow) INSPIRE PhD. students under INSPIRE Fellowship of the DST at these
Universities and Colleges. The recommendation of the Committee for international collaborations in this
respect has been noted and efforts would be made to realise the same.
Comments
The Committee takes note of thereby.
Recommendation
The Committee notes the improvement in the performance of some major universities/colleges.
However, the Committee is of the view that qualitative improvement is needed to make Indian universities
and research institutes at par with the international standards. International Best Practices need to be
inculcated in the tertiary education and higher research in India. It is, therefore, recommended that the
Ministry should take steps to meet these objectives. Financial support, technical and technological know-
how and R&D support should not be confined to a few major cities, and the requisite expertise and
knowledge must be disseminated to the remote areas of the country as it would help capture the untapped

7
knowledge resources in the country. The Ministry needs to bring about uniformity in the quality of
research conducted in institutions and universities spread across the country preferably by the end of
XII Five Year Plan. (Para 16.8)
Action Taken by Government
Many ongoing initiatives like Schemes related to R&D programme, Scheme for young Scientists,
Empowerment and Equity opportunities for excellence in Science, R&D "infrastructure augmentation
programes are targeting towards improvements of research qualities" at the Universities and research
Institutes in the country. Emphasis is always given to reach remotest corner of the country. However,
attempts are being made to strengthen this by disseminating this information so that we could tap
maximum resources of the country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee finds that many of the top universities have research Centres in collaboration with
other institutes in interdisciplinary fields. The Committee is of the view that many of the new technologies
coming out of these research centres would help in tackling the problems plaguing the country. In setting
up the Centres of Excellence, the Department should reach out to international institutions and seek more
project-based and targeted collaboration with foreign universities and research institutes. (Para 16.9)
Action Taken by Government
International collaborations with many academic institutions and research institutes of countries like
USA, UK, Japan, and France have already been made to initiate and implement joint collaborative research
activities. The research areas of collaboration are mostly Energy, Communication, and Bio-medical which
are interdisciplinary in nature. Efforts are being made to have more such collaborative projects with
International Partners.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
KNOWLEDGE INVOLVEMENT IN RESEARCH ADV ANCEMENT THROUGH NURTURING (KIRAN)
Recommendation
The Committee notes that there is a very small share of the women in the scientific R&D in the
country. The Committee feels that the Department and various institutes under it should also be forthcoming
in recruiting more female researchers and scientists into their organisation. While taking note of steady
increase in number of women scientists being supported under different schemes, the Committee feels that
the number is negligible. The Committee feels that the KIRAN being launched by the Department in place
of DISHA, should not only iron out the problems and difficulties but also empower women scientists to
develop and appropriate new technologies. (Para 17.6)

8
Action Taken by Government
KIRAN is not only handling problem and difficulties of women scientists but also empowering them
by implementing many more programmes in its ambit, such as, Women Scientist Scheme (covering R&D
Projects in basic Science and Engineering, societal based projects, and self employment), CURIE
(Consolidation of University Research through Innovation and Excellence in Women Universities)
Programme, Women Technology Parks, S&T for Women, Mobility Scheme etc.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee hopes that scheme for empowerment of women in its new form will not only iron
out the difficulties of women scientists but also address the crucial issues like mobility of women and
encourage them to pursue a career in scientific research as also for augmenting the women scientists pool
in the country. The Committee further notes that there has been a substantial increase in the amount of
fellowship for the women scientists under the KIRAN programme from 30,000 to 50,000 rupees. The
Committee observes that the fellowship under the new KIRAN scheme should be tax-free and should not
impose unnecessary pre-conditions in purchasing equipment and other products required for the research.
(Para 17.9)
Action Taken by Government
Department never put any pre-condition on Principal Investigators (PIs) of any project under
KIRAN for purchasing equipments, etc. Regarding Tax-free fellowship under KIRAN, the Department
is taking up the matter with Central Board of Direct Taxes, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
for clarification/exemption.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
SCHOLARSHIPS FOR RETAINING RESEARCH TALENT AND PROMOTION OF SCIENCE IN
THE COUNTRY
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken by the Ministry of Science & Technology that
have resulted in the inflow of accomplished researchers back to India. Measures taken by the three
Departments have led to the increasing reversal of flow of researchers. The Committee recommends that
further measures should be taken to retain bright Indian scientists coming back to India and attract the
young talents so that they find it more appealing to stay in India. For that purpose, the Department
should increase the scholarships and stipends provided to researchers. The Committee also recommends
that the research funding and grants should be linked to the potential and performance of the research
undertaken. The research undertaken should be incentivised, based on its utility and performance.
(Para 18.3)

9
Action Taken by Government
The Department is committed to attract the Indian brain from abroad and continue its attempt to
retain them to pursue world class research in Indian setting. The ongoing Ramanujan Fellowship of the
Department for brilliant scientists and engineers from all over the world to take up scientific research
positions in India has received utmost attention and the number of awards is increasing steadily. The
fellowship amount and the Research Grant had also been revised to make it more attractive. As viewed
by the Committee to increase the scholarship and stipend provided to researchers, the Government has
enhanced the fellowship of Junior Research Fellows, Senior Research Fellows and Research Associates
to the tune of 55.5% to 66.7% w.e.f. October, 2014. The Core Research Grant Scheme and Young
Scientist Project Scheme of the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) are linked to the
potential and performance of the research undertaken; and substantial funding is provided under these
Schemes. Track based research funding Scheme of the SERB is designed to support active scientists
based on their performance and utility of research.
Ministry of Science and Technology is currently implementing three such schemes namely Ramanujan
(by the DST), Ramalingaswami (by the DST) and INSPIRE Faculty Award (by the DST). While the
Ramanujan and Ramalingaswami are specially designed to attract the bright Indian Scientist for coming
back to India, INSPIRE Faculty Award, one of the components of the INSPIRE Programme of the
Department of Science and Technology is also attracted the bright young scientist (up-to 32 years of
age) to come back to India and start their research at any academic/research institutions in the country.
Though the initial efforts in this direction by this Ministry are encouraging, efforts to attract more bright
young scientists are underway so that these scientists could be able to sustain their research in globally
competitive environment.
Comments
The Department has only provided details of existing fellowships of the Ministry of Science
& Technology. It has not made any comment on suggestions put forth by the Committee in Para
18.3 that research funding and grants should be linked to the potential and performance of the
research undertaken. The Department has not responded to the recommendation of Committee
to work out some mechanism to incentivise research based on its utility and performance. The
Committee therefore as such re-iterates its observation/recommendation.
Recommendation
The Committee notes with serious concern the decline in the number of research publications in
journals and publications of national and international repute in various areas of scientific research. The
Committee also believes that there is no incentive or concrete action plan to promote such publications
by our scientists and researchers. The Committee is not satisfied with the policies pursued by the
Department to encourage the commercialisation of patents registered by the innovators. Necessary incentives
to researchers/innovators and scientists for the purpose should be put in place and purposively implemented.
(Para 18.4)

10
Action Taken by Government
The number of research publications emanating from India in various areas of scientific research
has witnessed an increasing trend. India's scientific publication output increased from 37502 in 2005 to
73099 in 2010 and 102753 in 2013. Accordingly, India's rank globally increased from 12th in 2005 to
9th in 2010 and further to 6th in 2013.
In view of the above, the statement of the committee that there is a decline in India's scientific
research publications over the years does not hold true and hence not accepted.
There are several incentives available to researchers to publish. Publications form an important
criteria for various research awards/fellowships etc. as well as consideration for future grants. The
department is evolving a track-based research grant scheme through Science and Engineering Research
Board, which envisages continuous research funding for 10 years for researcher consistently publishing
in high impact journals.
The Department has been implementing Patent Facilitation Programme under which the researchers
are facilitated to file the patent free of cost. So far 409 Indian patents (107 granted) and 23 International
patents (7 granted) have been filed on behalf of researchers from academic institutions. A policy for
providing incentives to the researchers/innovators on filing of patents is being evolved by Department
of Industrial Policy and Promotion. This department has suggested inclusion of several incentives including
career progression, research funding etc. in the proposed policy to encourage researchers/scientists to
actively participate in whole chain of Intellectual Property (IP) creation to commercialization.
With reference to the recommendation 18.4 of Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee,
NEB inputs are placed below:-
The Department has initiated many programmes to tap, recognize and support innovations across
the country. It conducts programmes on innovation in Private Public Partnership Mode such as Power
of Ideas, India Innovation Growth Programme (IIGP) and Business Plan Competitions in various institutions
in the country.
The IIGP has successfully evolved over year and positioned itself well in the Indian innovation
ecosystem. The IIGP has brought significant commercial value to the innovator/entrepreneur community.
As per an impact analysis report by Ernst & Young, the programme has been able to create an economic
value of over INR 1500 crores during the 2007-12 period. Over 350+ business engagement agreements
have been facilitated between participating innovators and the industry.
The Department implements institutional mechanism to support innovations such as Innovation &
Entrepreneurship Development Centre to support student driven innovative products. It also implements
flagship programme of Technology Business Incubators which nurtures technology based innovative
ideas and enables its commercialization through start-up and new venture creation. There are more than
70 Technology Business Incubators supported by DST and work in the area of Information Technology,
Bio Technology, Nano Technology, Design, Agriculture, Materials, etc. Further, it also provides Seed
support to deserving innovative start-ups under incubation for faster product development, validation and
commercialization.

11
The Technology Development Board of the Department also provides soft Capital/loans to technology
based innovative companies enabling them to scale up in the market. In view of the above programme
and initiatives focusing on innovations, the Department does not accept the recommendations as given
in Para 18.4.
Further, the Department is also in advanced talks with NITI Aayog for putting up a framework for
supporting grand challenges and creation of innovation hubs and world class incubation facilities to
support innovations across the country.
Comments
The Committee take note of the reply.
INCREASING PRIV ATE SECTOR INVESTMENT IN R&D
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the Department is striving to synchronise the efforts made by the public
sector with the private sector in the scientific research domain. However, such syncing process must take
into account the security of the 'common goods' and environmental concerns. Rather than focussing on
exemptions at the input levels, outputs should be incentivised. The partnership should be result oriented
and the benefits should be linked with the performance. (Para 19.5)
Action Taken by Government
The Department has noted the observations of the committee.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
NATIONAL MISSION FOR SUSTAINING THE HIMALAYAN ECOSYSTEM
Recommendation
The Committee hopes that National Mission for Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem, a part of National
Action Plan for Climate Change, will follow the Mission Document and its task forces will accomplish
the targets of the Mission. The Committee recommends that considering the enormous challenges of
Climate Change and fragile Himalayan ecology, this Mission should be adequately funded. (Para 20.8)
Action Taken by Government
The Department under its Climate Change Programme is coordinating National Mission for Sustaining
the Himalayan Ecosystem (NMSHE) under National Action Plan for Climate Change (NAPCC).
The point no. 20.8 of the recommendations of the PSC is accepted and following the NMSHE
document six nodal institutions have been identified to lead six thematic Task forces (TF). These are
TF-1 "Forest Resources and Plant Diversity" by G.B. Pant Institute of Himalayan Environment &
Development, (GBPIHED), Almora. TF-2 "Fauna and Wild Life Habitates" by Wildlife Institute of India,
(WII) Dehradun. TF-3 "Natural and Geological Wealth" by Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, (WHHG),

12
Dehra Dun. TF-4 "Water, Ice, Snow Resources including Glaciers" by National Institute of Hydrology,
(NIH), Roorkee. TF-5 "Traditional Knowledge System" by Jawaharlal Nehru University, (JNU), Delhi.
TF-6 "Himalayan Agriculture" by ICAR, New Delhi.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation
The focus of the Ministry of Science and Technology should be on endeavouring to acquire a global
leadership position in the frontier areas of sciences including material sciences, synthetic biology, genetics
and astrophysics, etc. International partnerships in these areas should be established with countries and
companies with known expertise and leadership in these and other areas of big ticket sciences.
(Para 20.9)
Action Taken by Government
Recommendation is accepted and necessary steps will be taken to comply.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Department should consider sharing their research and innovations with the state governments
and their instrumentalities so as to ensure a useful dissemination of knowledge throughout the country.
The Committee also recommends that special efforts should be made to disseminate information and
knowledge of the schemes of the Department in far-flung districts and particularly in the states of North
East. (Para 20.10)
Action Taken by Government
The Department is implementing State S&T Programme (SSTP) under which State S&T Councils
/Departments for Science and Technology (S&T) have been established in all States. The Department,
through this programme has been making conscious efforts to share scientific and technological outputs
emanating from DST's endeavour with State Governments through organizing All India/Regional meetings
of State Councils/Departments. The last all India meeting was organized by Gujarat State Council for
Science and Technology during 15th-16th September, 2014 at Gujarat Science City, Ahmedabad. Also,
a regional meeting on the specific issues of creation of Skill Development Centre for NE region was
organized at Assam State Council for Science and Technology, Guwahati on 21st January, 2015. Earlier
DST has shared technological outputs of Central S&T Agencies and Departments at the apex level in the
conferences of Chief Secretaries of States. A Technology Compendium on "Science, Technology and
Innovation-Potential uses for the State Governments" has also been prepared for dissemination to the
States. In line with the Parliamentary Standing Committee recommendation, the Department intends to
continue these activities vigorously to synergise efforts of DST and States. The next All India meeting
of State Councils/Departments has been planned in August, 2015 to disseminate the information and
knowledge of the schemes of the department to States/UTs.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science &
Technology, Environment & Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on
its behalf, present this Two Hundred Seventy-fourth Report on the Action Taken by the Department of
Biotechnology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Fifty-ninth Report of the Committee
on Demands for Grants (2015-2016) of the Department of Biotechnology, which was presented/laid in
both the Houses of Parliament on 7th May, 2015.
2. There were thirteenth recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Fifty-ninth Report of the
Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the
Department on 4th November, 2015.
3. In the meeting held on 15th January, 2016, the Committee considered the Report and adopted the
same.
N
EW D ELHI; ASHWANI KUMAR

Rajya Sabha.

TAC : Technical Appraisal Committee

(iv)

REPORT
INTRODUCTION
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Biotechnology on
the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Fifty-ninth Report of the Department-related
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands
for Grants (2015-16) of the Department of Biotechnology, presented to both the Houses of Parliament
on 7th May, 2015. There were thirteen recommendations in the Report of the Committee. Action Taken
notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on 4th November,
2015. The Department has intimated that it has accepted all the recommendations of the Committee. The
Committee, on examination of Action Taken Notes, however is not satisfied with action taken by the
Department in respect of two recommendations (para nos. 7.3 and 9.11) and would like the Department
to take further action in respect of these recommendations as indicated in the Report.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
Action Taken by the Department of Biotechnology are set out in the subsequent paragraphs:-
FINANCIAL ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE DEPARTMENT
Recommendation
The Committee feels that although the Department of Biotechnology had been able to spend 97.76
per cent and 99.19 per cent of the allocations made during 2012-13 and 2013-14, the allocation of the
Department were not only allocated on pro-rata basis during first three years of the Twelfth Plan period
but it has been reduced at RE stage in each of the first three years of the Plan period. The Committee
is of the considered view that the Biotechnology will play a very important role in the development of
the nation in the years to come and reduction in the allocations of the Department at the RE stage, when
the Department has demonstrated capability to utilize the allocated amounts, results in avoidable delay
in the implementation of programmes and achievement of the targets fixed, thereby adversely affecting
the scientific and technical advancement of the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
budgetary allocation of the Department should be increased at the RE stage during the current financial
year and the Department should be provided the full amount as it is capable of utilizing the same during
the remaining period of the Twelfth Plan. (Para 4.3)
Action Taken by Government
As a follow-up of this recommendation and the trend of expenditure as on September, 2015,
Department has communicated the demand of ` 150.00 Crores as additional grant at the Revised Estimate
(RE) stage to Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance for their consideration along with the
observation of the Parliamentary Standing Committee.

2
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Ministry of Finance would positively
consider the demand of the Department.
MONITORING MECHANISM OF THE DEPARTMENT
Recommendation
The Committee is of the view that a strong and potent monitoring mechanism is extremely important
for achieving the set objectives and implementation of the schemes and, therefore, recommends that the
Department should continue with its monitoring mechanisms to ensure that there are no time and cost
overruns in respect of its schemes / programmes. (Para 5.2)
Action Taken by Government
The Department noted the recommendation to continue its monitoring mechanisms to avoid time
and cost overruns. Therefore, in large projects involving multiple agencies additionally Project Management
and Monitoring Committees have been constituted which besides site visits monitors physical technical
and financial achievements of individual components of the project.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee notes that inspite of making utilization of its allocated funds in respect of Research
and Development scheme, the allocation under R&D had been considerably reduced during the 2014-
15. The apparent increase in allocation during 2015-16 is actually due to merger of 'International
Collaboration' under R&D scheme. The Committee is of the view that for facilitating R&D and
encouraging young scientists in the extremely important area of biotechnology, increased allocations to
this sector are in order. Genomics, synthetic biology and chemical biology are frontier areas of big ticket
science and for India to establish itself as a global leader in these areas, funds should never be an issue.
We need to invest in our future now. Biotechnology holds the key to some of the critical challenges that
we face. (Para 6.4)
Action Taken by Government
Department remains encouraged at the recognition of importance of increase investments in
biotechnology R&D for pursuing cutting edge technologies. As detailed in action taken report for
recommendation 4.3, additional budget has been requested for consideration by Ministry of Finance at
RE stage.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. Since biotechnology holds the key to some of our critical
challenges, the Committee hopes that the Department would be able to convince the concerned
authorities in Finance Ministry for increase in allocation for R&D at RE stage.

3
PRIV ATE SECTOR INVESTMENT IN RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken by Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance
Council (BIRAC) to encourage and involve the private sector in the field of Biotechnology. The
Committee is of the view that involving / facilitating private sector is extremely important for accelerating
the growth of biotechnology in the country and recommends that BIRAC should accelerate its efforts to
attract / facilitate private sector participation and increase global competitiveness of Indian biotech
industry. International partnership should be entered in the frontier area of biotechnology and the results
thereof should be clearly verifiable. (Para 7.3)
Action Taken by Government
The recommendation has been communicated to BIRAC for accelerating the efforts in accordance
with the directions of the Committee.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the fact that BIRAC has been intimated for accelerating the
efforts in accordance with the directions of the Committee. But the Committee feels that what
action BIRAC has taken in pursuance of the recommendation of the Committee, has not been
communicated. The Committee therefore is of the view that action taken by BIRAC needs to
be intimated.
PROGRAMME FOR PROMOTION OF EXCELLENCE AND INNOV ATION
Recommendation
The Committee notes the reasons for underutilization of allocated funds for 'Programme for Promotion
of Excellence and Innovation' during 2014-15 and feels that they are of administrative nature and that
underutilization of funds was avoidable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department
should strengthen its administrative and monitoring mechanisms to ensure that funds allocated for
important projects are not underutilized. (Para 8.4)
Action Taken by Government
The concerned Programme Division has already undertaken appropriate steps to ensure that the
funds allocated for Centres of Excellence scheme are fully utilized. An advertisement for fresh call for
proposals from institution / universities has been made. 32 proposals have been shortlisted after scrutiny
on techno-economic feasibility by Technical Appraisal Committee (TAC) of experts. Therefore, additional
budget has also been requested at R.E. stage from Ministry of Finance for funding of these proposals
at cutting edge of excellence.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be informed of the progress made in the
above direction during the consideration of Demands for Grants 2016-17 of the Department.

4
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (HRD)
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the allocation for Human Resource Development at the RE stage has
remained almost the same during the last three years. Although the Department was not able to fully
utilize the allocation made to the programme during 2013-14, it could utilized most of the outlays during
2012-13 and 2014-15. The Committee notes the schemes initiated by the Department to attract and
develop quality human resource skilled and quality manpower is an important and key component for
scientific development in multidisciplinary areas of biotechnology. The Committee, recommends that the
Department should be allocated additional funds for this sector to ensure completion of schemes initiated
for scientific development in multidisciplinary areas of biotechnology. The Committee also recommends
that the Department on its own part, should ensure that funds allocated for Human Resource Development
are utilized not only fully but optimally. (Para 9.9)
Action Taken by Government
Department is highly encouraged on the recognition to the schemes of Human Resource Development.
As mentioned in Action Taken to recommendation 4.3, an additional budgetary requirement of ` 30.00
Crores has been proposed at R.E. stage for consideration by Ministry of Finance.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee notes with concern the reasons outlined by the Secretary, Department of Biotechnology
for not-filling top posts in scientific institutions. The Committee is of the view that the situation that
has arisen due to retirement age of scientists in universities vis-a-vis the Department's institutes needs
to be rectified to create a good research base in the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Department should evolve a suitable mechanism to contain this problem of brain drain from institutes
to universities and adhocism. Considering the actual role of experts in the field of biotechnological
advance and also the need for the best minds to provide a leadership role in the area, the challenges
outlined above need to be proactively and imaginatively dealt with. Hence retaining and engaging the
best minds is of critical importance. (Para 9.11)
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Committee have been followed up in some cases of autonomous institutions
with required results.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. However, the Committee would like, as per its
recommendation, to be apprised of the details of the mechanism evolved in this regard.

5
INDIA'S RANKING IN INTERNATIONAL RESEARCH PUBLICATIONS
Recommendation
The Committee notes the improvement in the global ranking of the country in various fields of
Biotechnology but expresses its concern over India lagging behind China in the field of foundational
sciences. The Committee also notes that the Department has not let the budgetary constraints come into
the way of its excelling in the field of biotechnology and earning India a place in the top countries of
the world. The Committee exhorts the Department to attain excellence and improve India's global ranking
in Biotechnology and must specifically endeavor to be amongst the first five countries as per established
parameters. A time frame for achieving the milestone should be fixed and a purposive / concrete Action
Plan be formulated to achieve this ambitious national aspiration. The Committee feels that Department
should adore the number of patents granted to its scientists as one of the measures to judge the quality
of research. This area requires a special focus. Commercialization of patents is a week area. The reasons
therefore need to be identified and suitable correctives should be applied. (Para 10.4)
Action Taken by Government
Department has noted the recommendation and has made efforts to draft a new Biotechnology
Development Strategy for achieving the goals. The patent facilitation cell in DBT and interface between
BIRAC and DBT project investigators from public sector have also been strengthened for increased
public private partnership and product development.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that action taken by the Department would yield
the desired results.
STEPS TO CONTAIN BRAIN DRAIN
Recommendation
The Committee notes the steps taken by the Department for attracting the required talent available
with the country in the field of Biotechnology through various fellowships / schemes, both for students
and scientists. The Committee feels that there is no dearth of talent in the country. The need is to tap
this talent and provide all necessary wherewithal for achieving excellence in the field of Biotechnology.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that there should be no let up in the efforts of the Department
to attract talented people in the field of Biotechnology. The Department should spearhead an accelerated
efforts not only to woo the talent available in the country but also attract top Indian talent in other
countries to the field of Biotechnology in India. Apart from initiatives already in place, the Department
should explore other meaningful initiatives to establish strong foundations for an onward and long
journey to achieve a leadership role in the various areas of biotechnology. The Committee feels that
excellent leadership has been provided in the past by the Department of Biotechnology but for the
Department to play its rightful role in meeting challenges of the future, it must inspire the best minds

6
to join the Department and continue with various schemes. Allocating fiscal and career progression
related incentives should be put in place for the purpose. (Para 11.5)
Action Taken by Government
The Recommendation has been discussed in the Scientific Advisory Committee (overseas) of DBT
and also in the Scientific Advisory Committee in each of the autonomous institutions. Accordingly, the
schemes such as centres of Excellence, Ramalingswami Fellowships, Welcome Trust - DBT Alliance
Programme and Network have been strengthened with new opportunities for career development. Additional
efforts are planned for 2016-17, depending on availability of funds.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and feels that details of schemes strengthened may
be provided.
BIOTECHNOLOGY FOR SOCIETAL DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee notes the contributions made by the Department in the field of bio-fertilizer production,
vermicomposting, apiculture, poultry, fish production and rearing, artificial insemination, mushroom
cultivation, goat rearing, fruit plant nurseries, sericulture, post-harvest processing technologies, hybrid
seed production, use of quality planning materials and women and child health care for societal development
through biotechnology. The Committee recommends that the Department should ensure greater involvement
of Civil Society organizations, NGOs, local representatives at the Panchayat level in the implementation
of its schemes / programmes so that the benefits of the programmes percolate to the rural areas and
weaker and lower sections of the society in real terms.
The Committee notes that although the Department has outlined the multifarious benefits of the
programme, the fact remains that, in spite of its earlier assurance to the Committee to undertake the
survey to assess its impact as to how it actually helped / benefitted society in terms of employment and
entrepreneurship, the survey has not been conducted so far. The Committee recommends that the Department
should institute a survey to assess the impact of its societal benefit programmes / schemes in actual terms
and report the results to the Committee. (Para nos. 12.7 & 12.8)
Action Taken by Government
This programme is implemented to help the community for the socio-economic upliftment through
training and demonstrations activities in biotech based interventions through diffusion of proven and field
tested technologies. The aim of this programme is to support socially relevant activities to demonstrate
the R&D leads and delivery of the technological know-how for the benefit of the community through
self-help groups, science based NGOs and Rural Universities.
The programme is implemented as competitive grant system similar to R&D scheme. A special
committee of experts, social workers and eminent rural leaders is operational for need assessment,
project appraisal and monitoring. All the beneficiaries submit regular progress reports and make presentations

7
on yearly-basis to special committee. The implementations of these schemes have been regularly reviewed
with a strong monitoring and assessment mechanism of the department. Also the schemes/ projects are
being regularly monitoring through the Task Force mechanism and site visits by the experts, wherever
essential. With this the actual deliverables have been assured to assess the benefits to the end users for
the upliftment of the target community.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
GENERAL
Recommendation
The Committee also recommends that special efforts should be made to disseminate information and
knowledge of the schemes of the Department in far flung districts and particularly in the states of North
East. (Para 12.9)
Action Taken by Government
Under the Departmental scheme of North-Eastern Region- Biotechnology Programme Management
Cell (NER-BPMC) large funding is being provided both for R&D and diffusion of technology relevant
to the North-Eastern region through dissemination of appropriate technological intervention and knowledge
gain to the target community. This is to provide extensive benefits to the north eastern states in India
by mandatory 10% funding of the DBT Gross Budgetary Support as a policy measure. With the diffusion
of technological know-how, benefits, have been provided to the educated youths, women SHGs and to
the farmers by undertaking various income and self-employment generation activities for the socio-
economic upliftment in the North-Eastern region.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the steps taken by the Government to disseminate information
and knowledge of schemes in the states of North East would help in the socio-economic upliftment
of the people of these states.
Recommendation
Parliamentary oversight through the work of the Standing Committee would be meaningful only if
the recommendation of the Committee are implemented in their true spirit and not ignored under the usual
pretexts. The Committee hopes that the Recommendation made are implemented proactively and within
a stipulated time frame. (Para 12.10)
Action Taken by Government
The Department assures that the recommendations are implemented in true spirit and shall report the
challenges to the Committee during implementation for suggestions.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

INTRODUCTION 
 
 I, the Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Science & Technology, Environment & Forests, having been authorised by the 
Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this Two Hundred Seventy-fifth 
Report on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences on the recommendations 
contained in Two Hundred Sixty Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2015-
2016) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which was presented laid in  the both the Houses 
of Parliament on 7th May, 2015. 
 
2. There were Twenty recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Sixty Report 
of the Committee.  Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were 
received from the Ministry on 21st July, 2015.

Report and adopted the same.

REPORT 
 
The report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry 
of Earth Sciences on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Sixtieth 
Report of the Department -related Parliamentary Stand ing Committee on Science 
& Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2015 -2016) of 
the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which was presented to both the Houses of 
Parliament on 7 th May, 2015. There were twenty -four recommendations in the 
Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the 
Committee was received from the Ministry on 2 1st  July, 2015. The Ministry has 
intimated that it has accepted all the recommendations of the Committee. The 
Committee, on examination of Ac tion Taken Notes, however is not satisfied with 
action taken by the Ministry in respect of one recommendation (para 6.2)  and 
would like the Ministry to take further action in respect of such recommendations 
as indicated in the Report. 
 The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of 
the Committee on the action taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences are set out in 
the succeeding paragraphs:- 
FINANCIAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS FOR THE EARTH 
COMMISSION 
Recommendation (Para 4.3) 
The Comm ittee feels that without the devolution of financial and 
administrative power to the Earth Commission, the functioning of the Ministry 
seriously gets hampered. The Committee reiterates the recommendation made in 
its 243rd Report that immediate measures sho uld be taken to devolve financial and 
administrative power to the Earth Commission for its effective functioning.  
Action Taken by Government 
A  note for the Cabinet for giving financial and administrative powers to 
the Earth Commission, on the lines of Sp ace Commission and Atomic Energy 
Commission, was submitted to the Cabinet Secretariat for necessary action with 
the approval of the then Hon'ble Minister for Earth Sciences.  In reply, as advised, 
inter-ministerial consultations with relevant Ministries/De partment were carried 
out.  All relevant Ministries/Departments had supported the proposal.  However, 
D/Expenditure had raised certain observations which were examined in the 
Ministry.  Accordingly, with the approval of Hon'ble Minister for Earth Sciences 
on 24th December, 2014 the comments of the Ministry to these observations have 
been sent to D/Expenditure on 9 th February, 2015 with the request to convey their 
approval to the proposal to enable this Ministry to prepare revised Note for the 
Cabinet and su bmit to the Cabinet Secretariat for necessary approvals.  The 
approval of D/Expenditure is still awaited.  
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to be further apprised of 
the development in this regard. 
FINANCIAL ACHIEVEMENTS OF MINISTRY-AN ANALYSIS OF 
TREND OF UTILISATION 
Recommendation (Para 5.2) 
 The Committee observes that in the last three years, B.E. allocation has 
been reduced at the RE level.  The Committee takes strong exception to such 
reduction which causes unnecessary delay i n the completion of 

programmes/projects.  The Committee, therefore, recommends to avoid 
curtailment of funds at RE stage which has been a regular trend in all the years and 
which severely hampers the programmes/projects.   
Action Taken by Government 
 The o bservations of the Committee have been noted with 
acknowledgement. 
Comments    
 The Committee recommends that the steps taken to avoid curtailment 
of funds at RE stage may be communicated. 
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2015-16 
Recommendation (Para 6.2) 
 The Committee observes that there has been a drastic reduction in the 
budgetary allocation in the financial year 2015 -16 to the tune of Rs. 79.30 crore 
which is a serious blockade in taking up new activities/initiatives by the Ministry 
for whi ch additional finds of Rs. 371 crore are required.  The Committee 
recommends that efforts be made by the Ministry by prudently utilizing the given 
allocated budget and by planning and targeting the missions and programmes in an

Action Taken by Government 
 The observations of the Committee have been noted with 
acknowledgement. 
Comments    
 The Committee has not been informed of the concrete action taken by 
the Government in pursuance of the above recommendation and would like 
to be apprised of the same. 
RATIONALIZATION OF THE SCHEMES 
Recommendation (Para 7.4) 
 The Committee expresses its unhappiness that for most of the programmes 
there has been a reduction in the budgetary allocation including the programme of 
High Performance Computing wh ich is an important programme of the ministry. 
The Committee feels that reduction in the number of programmes the budgetary 
reduction in allocation of programmes after clubbing them together will not ensure 
rationalisation of expenditure as the funds requi red for the programme will not be 
sufficient enough to meet the expenses of the programmes. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that along with clubbing of programmes, adequate funds 
should also be allocated to ensure efficient functioning. 
Action Taken by Government 
 The observations of the Committee have been noted with 
acknowledgement.  It is submitted that due to reduction in BE, several new 
activities/programs are forced to be deferred including the HPC.  It is also 
submitted that efforts have been ma de by the Ministry for consideration of 
additional fund of Rs. 371 crore at the RE stage for ensuring efficient overall 
functioning of the Ministry.  
Comments  
 The Committee notes the reply.    
POLAR SCIENCES AND CRYOSPHERE 
Recommendation (Para 8.7) 
 The Committee is of the view that the programme is one of the most 
important programmes of the Ministry and the activities pursued in the Antarctica, 

Arctic and Himalayan region is of extreme use for better understanding of Indian 
Climate and other societal be nefits. The Committee also observes that the 
programme is of strategic importance and in order to make our country’s presence 
in Arctic and Antarctica felt, this programme is of utmost importance.  The 
research undertaken in polar regions will help underst and the fragile Himalayan 
region. The Committee recommends that the programme should be undertaken 
diligently and in a well-planned manner.   
Action Taken by Government 
 Polar Science programme is undertaken diligently and the activities and 
their schedule are progressing in well-planned manner. 
Comments   
  The Committee notes the reply.

SEISOMOLGICAL AND GEOSCIENCE (SAGE) PROGRAMME 
Recommendation (Para 10.7) 
 The Committee takes note of the activities undertaken in the preparatory 
phase which is relevant for collect ing seismological data and for continuing the 
seismological research activities in the main phase. The Committee recommends 
that the main phase of the programme be carried on taking inputs from preparatory 
phase and to complete the deep drilling of the bor e holes essential for 
understanding the regular occurrence of the earthquakes in the region.   
Action Taken by Government 
 Based on the preparatory studies the location of the pilot boreholes has 
been fixed.  Also the information gathered from the shallow deep boe boles will be 
used as the input to undertake the pilot borehole drilling as well as to carry out the 
measurements.  
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply. 
Recommendation (Para 10.8) 
 The Committee takes serious note of the fact that additiona l Rs. 48 crore is 
required and only meagre amount of Rs. 4 crore are available to the Ministry for 
such an important programme which is critical in nature seeing the regular 

occurrence of earthquakes in the region. The Committee recommends that 
ensuring fu nds to the programme should be a high priority as the research on 
earthquakes will serve two purposes of monitoring critical parameters in the “near 
field” of earthquakes and providing India a unique opportunity to take global 
leadership role in this important scientific issue.  
Action Taken by Government 
 Subsequent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee meeting the total 
allocation of Seismology and Geosciences (SAGE) has been re -
organized/readjusted for different components and an amount of Rs. 20 crore  has 
now been allocated for Koyna deep drilling.  The remaining required funds will be 
sought through the supplementary at RE stage.  
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Ministry would be 
allocated required funds at the RE Stage.

 The Committee notes that the Ministry created a National Centre for 
Seismology as an attached office of the Ministry of Earth Sciences. The 
Committee also takes note of the fact that the separatio n of manpower,

Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply.  Further action taken in the matter by 
the concerned authority should be intimated to the Committee.  
MICROZONATION OF CITIES 
Recommendation (Para 12.2) 
 The Committee takes note of the importance of microzonation of cities on 
account of vulnerability of India’s land to severe earthquakes and recommends to 
Government to take such purposive measures in consultation with State 
Governments and stakeholders as would mitigate the consequences of a potential 
earthquake in the vulnerable areas. The Committee also recommends that 
microzonation of cities particularly those fa lling in seismic zone V, IV and III 
should be taken up expeditiously and necessary geophysical, geological and other 
information/data should be acquired from Geological Survey of India so that delay 
in microzonation of cities is avoided.  
Action Taken by Government 
 Necessary action would be taken as per the recommendation of 
Parliamentary Standing Committee. 
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised of the 
developments in the matter.

ACCURACY IN WEATHER FORECASTING  
Recommendation (Para 17.7) 
 The Committee notes the improvement in the accuracy of weather 
predictions including the predictions of the recent flash floods in J&K. The 
Committee feels t hat the accuracy in prediction of weather depends upon the 
augmentation in High Computing Systems. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the accuracy be improved further to bring it at par with other 
nations.  The Committee further recommends that allo cation of adequate funds to 
improve the infrastructure needed to enhance the accuracy of weather predictions 
including augmentation of High Computing Systems be ensured.  
Action Taken by Government 
 The Ministry thanks the Parliament Standing Committee for  its 
appreciation and acknowledgment of improvement in weather prediction.   
Towards this direction the Ministry has made considerable efforts in upgrading the 
HPC facility existing in MoES units to 1.2 peta flops.  With this augmentation of 
HPC, global mo dels with horizontal resolution of about 17 km and regional 
models with a horizontal resolution of 1.5 km will be run which would 
resolve/predict the embedded mesoscale weather systems in a better manner.  This 
will also enable running of higher resolution  model ensemble prediction system 
with more number of members for generating probabilistic forecasts.  However to 
continuously improve these forecasts there is a need for continuous augmentation 
of HPC to 7 -10 P flops for which Cabinet has given approval a t an estimated 
budget of Rs.569.69 crores.  As per the requirement, appropriate allocation of 
funds will be made. 
Comments    
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should prioritise the 
work for augmentation of High Performance Computing to 7 -10  P fl ops and 
seek requisite funds for which Cabinet has given approval. 
Recommendation (Para 17.9) 
 The Committee recommends to the Ministry to come out with an action 
plan on how the Ministry is dealing with changing climatic variability in various 
fields such  as agriculture, disaster management etc. The Committee further 
recommends that the additional funds required i.e. Rs. 14 crore should be made 
available to the Ministry for installing the system for the improvement of air 
quality forecasts in Ahmedabad and Mumbai.  
Action Taken by Government 
 Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (ESSO -IITM) under the Ministry 
through the activities of Centre for Climate Change Research (CCCR)  is doing 
extensive research work on climate variability and its impact on var ious sectors on 
agriculture, water resources, disaster management etc.  ESSO -IITM has developed 
an Earth System Model which provides high -resolution regional climate change 
scenarios to the Ministry of Environment and Forests for impact assessment 
studies.  The concerned ministries make use of these scenarios for mitigation 
purposes.  During the next 5 -10 years, ESSO -IITM will fully develop test and 
validate the Earth System Model (ESM) with regard to simulation of the global 
climate including the Indian an d Asian monsoons, coupled climate phenomena 
like ENSO, IOD, Pacific and Atlantic decadal variability, etc.  This will be used to 

give high resolution projections of future monsoon climate required for various 
impact assessment studies (eg., climate, water resources, agriculture, health, etc.) 
Steps have been taken by the Ministry for additional funds of Rs. 371 crore at the 
RE stage which includes Rs. 14 crore for System for Air Quality Forecasting and 
Research (SAFAR) programme. 
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and stresses that Ministry should 
continue its extensive research and studies on changing climatic variability 
and its impact. 
MODERNISATION OF INDIAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT 
Recommendation (Para 18.4) 
 The Committee is of the opinion tha t the Modernisation of Indian 
Meteorological Department is of utmost importance and should be taken up 
earnestly. The Committee, however, expresses serious concern on the fact that the 
modernisation of IMD – Phase II has not been taken up due to non -availability of 
funds.  The Committee feels that in view of dependability of farmers on the rains 
for agriculture and the unpredictable weather changes because of climatic 
variability and increasing magnitude of natural disasters in the country, the 
modernisation of IMD is imperative for correct prediction. The Committee, 
therefore, makes strong recommendation that the Ministry should make all efforts 
to initiate Phase II of Modernisation of IMD and merely because of the funds 
crunch, the programme should not suffer.  
Action Taken by Government 
 The observations of the Committee are gratefully acknowledged.  Keeping 
in view the paucity of grants the targeted activities are prioritized in terms of:- 
(i) Himalayan Meteorology Program. 
(ii) Integrated Meteorology Services for NE region. 
(iii) Priority Augmentation of Doppler Weather Radar Network from the 
allocations so far made to the Ministry during XII Plan. 
The Modernization Phase-II of IMD is essentially required at estimated cost 
of Rs. 1305 crores for augmentation and enhance ment of various observation 
systems as per requirement over different parts of the country.   Preliminary works 
including identification of sites, preparation of Detailed Project Report, 
Expenditure Finance Committee documents have been prepared and the pr oject 
can be implemented as soon as approval is accorded by the Government. 
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and recommends that the Ministry 
should pursue the matter for early approval to the proposal. 
AGRO - METEOROLOGICAL SERVICES 
Recommendation (Para 19.5) 
 The Committee observes that weather forecasts are being disseminated to 
the farmers through SMSs/Mobile technology and the outreach of agromet 
services to 8 million farmers and to selected districts. The Committee notes that 
the improvement in forecasts has not been satisfactory at sub district scale which 
needs to be improved by installing weather observing networks. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends to improve the forecast at the sub district level and also to 
increase the outreach from  the district level to the block level. The Committee 
further recommends to increase the number of farmers to 10 million receiving the 
agro met services from the Ministry and in this regard, the Ministry should 

continue its coordination efforts and discuss ions with other related 
agencies/institutions and the setting up of District Agro Meteorological Units 
should be taken up to enhance the dissemination of agro-advisories to farmers.    
Action Taken by Government 
 The observations of the Committee are grate fully acknowledged.  The 
number of registered farmers to receive crops specific farm advisories now stands 
at 10.24 million and efforts are on with the partners to enhance it further so as to 
assist the farming community by all means.   Pilot mode efforts are made to 
develop sub -district scale forecasts wherever sub -district scale surface 
observatories as well as Automatic Weather Station (AWS), Automatic Rain 
Gauges (ARG) and other meteorological networks are available. 
 ESSO-IMD is actively coordinating w ith Indian Council for Agriculture 
Research (ICAR) for setting up of District Agrometeorological Units (DAUMUs) 
at Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs).  In first phase, ~50 KVKs have been identified 
to work as DAMU which is likely to be rolled out in FY 2015 -16 in preparation as 
well as dissemination of block level agromet advisories to the farmers in the 
respective block. 
Comments  
 The Committee notes the reply.

Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply.  
RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND TRAINING OUTREACH  
Recommendation (Para 21.6) 
 The Committee notes the importance of trained manpower and coordination 
in research activities including international cooperation. The Committee observes 
that the setting up of Institute for Operational Oceanography is still not complete 
and requires more time. The Committee further notes that the paucity of funds is 
becoming the major obstacle in ensuring the extramural activities an d fulfilling the 
objectives of the programme.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
additional funds needed for the programme should be sought by the Ministry to 
ensure continuation of research and extra mural activities. The Committee further 
recommends that the Institute for Operational Oceanography should be set up in 
the scheduled time frame.  
 
 

Action Taken by Government 
 Under the program on "Research, Education, Training and Outreach 
"various activities including extra -mural support, capacity bu ilding programms, 
International cooperation etc are undertaken.  The International oceanography 
being established at ESSO-INCOIS Hyderabad at a total estimated cost of Rs. 100 
crore is partially functional using the existing infrastructure available at ESS O-
INCOIS. 
 In general the program is moving as per the expected timelines, however 
there has been some delay in establishing the physical structures including 
technical buildings and hostel due to paucity of funds.  Notwithstanding this, some 
academic activities have been initiated using the present INCOIS set up. 
 State of art E -class room facility under the Institute of Operational 
Oceanography Program has been operational sine March, 2015.  The centre has so 
far successfully trained 297 trainees includin g 52 from 22 countries abroad, 
through 5 International and 6 National programmes. 
 However to make the centre fully operational, it is essential that the 
physical infrastructure is in place at the earliest. 
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and re commends that the resources 
required for making the Institute for Operational Oceanography fully 
functional should be made available to the Ministry.   
ENVIRONMENT MONITORING AND RESEARCH 
Recommendation (Para 22.3) 
 The Committee notes that the Ministry is  having a coordination mechanism 
with the Central Pollution Control Board to measure the concentrations of various 
pollutants over the Delhi region. The Committee, however, feels that coordination 
between the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Chang e and the Ministry 
of Earth Sciences needs to be improved further so as to monitor changes related to 
climate and the efficient coordination mechanism will speed up the 
studies/activities related to combating the environmental degradation and effects 
of pollution.   
Action Taken by Government 
 ISSO-IITM is coordinating with t he Ministry of Environment,  Forest and 
Climate Change and t he data from the SAFAR system set up by ESS O-IITM are 
being shared with that  Ministry on real time basis for national monitori ng of air 
quality. 
 SAFAR data provides region -specific health impact assessments within 
megacity during control and extreme air pollution conditions.  The short lived 
greenhouse pollutants have substantial effects on agriculture, human health, 
natural biosphere, aviation and surface transport industry due to winter fog in the 
Indo-Gangetic plain.  However , there are substantial research gaps in these areas 
which can be addressed by coordinated interaction of scientists of SAFAR and 
CPCB to combat the environmental degradation and effects of pollution.  
Comments    
 The Committee notes the reply and recommends that all necessary 
steps should be taken by SAFAR and C entral Pollution Control Board to 
bridge the stated research gaps.  
Recommendation (Para 22.4) 

 The Committee recommends that special efforts should be made to 
disseminate information and knowledge of the schemes of the Ministry in far flung 
districts and particularly in the states of North East. 
Action Taken by Government 
 Dissemination information  and knowledge of Ministry's schemes (Earth 
Sciences) were made in ten districts of six NE states (viz. Manipur, Meghalaya, 
Assam, Mizoram, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh) and four far flung districts of 
Kerala and Gujarat during 2014-15. 
 Further, efforts are continued for disseminating information and state of art 
knowledge of schemes of Ministry on various topics of Earth Sciences like Geo -
Hazards (Earth -quake etc.), Atmosphere (Cyclone, monsoon, Agro -advisories, 
etc.),  Ocean (Tsunami, Potential Fishing Zon e, resources, etc.)  in far flung 
districts and states of North -East through exhibition on wheel and enhancing and 
support to seminar/workshops etc.  
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply.
